extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical mechanics / readers of Newton's Principia (Latin)
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of propositions and lemmas from a Latin edition of Newton's Principia (De Motu Corporum), giving precise theorems about mutual attraction, spherical shells, and how composite spherical bodies attract interior/exterior points. Useful for deriving shell theorems and orbital perturbation results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corol. 22 (nodal motion & mass distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Et inde vicissim, ex motu nodorum innotescit constitutio globi. Nimirum si globus polos eosdem constanter servat, & motus fit in antecedentia, materia juxta aequatorem redundat; si in consequentia, deficit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how redistribution of mass (e.g., accumulation of matter near equator or poles) affects motion of nodes and reveals the globe's constitution; gives constructive argument using impulses and composition of motions to show axis inclination and rotation invariance, and how added mass (mountains) perturbs rotation causing pole wandering unless placed at poles or equator or compensated by opposite additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXVII (THEOREMA XXVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positis iisdem attractionum legibus, dico quod corpus exterius S, circa interiorum P, T commune gravitatis centricm O, radiis ad centrum illud ductis, describit areas temporibus magis proportionales & orbem ad formam ellipseos umbilicum in centro eodem habentis magis accedentem, qtiam circa corpus intimum & maximum T, radiis ad ipsum ductis describere potest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that under the same attraction laws an external body S orbiting the common center of gravity O of interior bodies P and T describes areas more nearly proportional to times and orbits more nearly elliptical (with umbilicus at that center) than if it were orbiting merely the inner/maximum body T. Proof uses composition of attractions of internal bodies and comparison of inverse-square dependences.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXVIII (THEOREMA XXVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Positis iisdem attractionum legibus, dico quod corpus exterius S circa interiorum Y & T commune gravitatis centrum O, radiis ad centrum illic ductis, describit areas temporibus magis proportionales, & orbem ad formam ellipseos umbilicum in centro eodem habentis magis accedentem, si corpus intimurn & maximum his attractionibus perinde atque cetera agitetur, quam si id vel non attractum quiescat, vel multo magis aut multo minus attractum aut multo magis aut multo minus agitetur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A refinement of LXVII addressing perturbations: if interior bodies move under mutual attractions appropriately the external body's motion more closely approximates Keplerian area law and elliptical form with center at common center of gravity; gives argument about perturbation magnitude depending on motion of interior masses and common-center motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXIX (THEOREMA XXIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: In systemate corporum plurium A, B, C, D, &c. si corpori aliquod A trahit caetera omnia B, C, D, &c. viribus acceleratricibus quae sunt reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum a trahente; & corpus aliud B trahit etiam caetera A, C, D, &c. viribus quae sunt reciproce ut quadrata distantiarum a trahente: erunt absolute corporum trahentium A, B vires ad invicem, ut sunt ipsa corpora A, B, quocumque sunt vires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates that when mutual attractive (accelerative) forces between bodies follow an inverse-square law with distance, the absolute forces with which two bodies attract each other are in the ratio of their masses (i.e., bodies act on one another in proportion to their 'massae'). Corollaries extend this to systems and other distance-laws (direct or other power laws).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium on attraction and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: His propositionibus manuducimur ad analogiam inter vires centripetas, & corpora centralia, ad quse vires illae dirigi solent. Rationi enim consentaneum est, ut vires, quse ad corpora diriguntur, pendeant ab eorundem natura & quantitate...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses interpreting 'attraction' generally as any tendency of bodies to approach (action at a distance, emission of spirits, pressure by fluids, magnetic-like forces), and sets out the mathematical program: quantify forces and proportions first, then compare with phenomena to ascertain physical causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXX (THEOREMA XXX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad sphaericæ superficiei puncta singula tendant vires aequales centripetæ decrescentes in duplicata ratione distantiarum a punctis: dico quod corpusculum intra superficiem constitutum his viribus nullam in partem attrahitur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The shell theorem interior case: if each point of a spherical surface exerts an equal central force decreasing as inverse square of distance, a particle inside the hollow sphere experiences zero net force. Proof partitions the surface into equal annuli and shows pairwise cancellation of opposite attractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXI (THEOREMA XXXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lisdem positis, dico quod corpusculum extra sphaericam superficiem constitutum attrahitur ad centrum sphaeræ vi reciproce proportionali quadrato distantice suæ ab eodem centro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shell theorem exterior case: a particle outside a spherical shell is attracted as if all the shell's mass were concentrated at its center, i.e., force ∝ 1/(distance)^2. The proof constructs equal surface elements and relates their contributions to a model circular element whose effect is proportional to area and inverse-square distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXII (THEOREMA XXXII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad sphaeræ cujusvis puncta singula tendant vires æquales centripetæ decrescentes in duplicata ratione distantiarum a punctis; ac detur tum sphaeræ densitas, tum ratio diametri sphaeræ ad distantiam corpusculi a centro ejus: dico quod vis, qua corpusculum attrahitur, proportionalis erit semidiametro sphaeræ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives relation between sphere density/size and force: when forces of surface elements obey inverse-square, and given sphere density and ratio of diameter to particle distance, the attractive force a sphere exerts on a particle (in certain comparative setups) is proportional to the semi-diameter; corollaries relate periodic times to proportional distances/diameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXIII (THEOREMA XXXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad sphaeræ alicujus datæ puncta singula tendant æquales vires centripetæ decrescentes in duplicata ratione distantiarum a punctis: dico quod corpusculum intra sphaeram constitutum attrahitur vi proportionali distantice suæ ab ipsius centro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that for a solid homogeneous sphere made of such concentric shells, the net force on an interior point is proportional to its distance from the center (i.e., linear restoring force — harmonic oscillator behavior). Proof removes outer concentric shells (which cancel) leaving only the inner sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXIV (THEOREMA XXXIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lisdem positis dico quod corpusculum extra sphaeram constitutum attrahitur vi reciproce proportionali quadrato distantice suæ ab ipsius centro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restates and generalizes shell theorem: the total attraction of a homogeneous sphere on an external particle follows inverse-square dependence on distance from center; argument by composing concentric spherical layers whose contributions sum in inverse-square fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXV (THEOREMA XXXV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad sphaeræ datæ puncta singula tendant vires æquales centripetæ decrescentes in duplicata ratione distantiarum a punctis; dico quod sphaera quævis alia similaris ab eadem attraheret vi reciproce proportionali quadrato distantice centrorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States that any two similar homogeneous spheres attract each other as if their masses were concentrated at their centers, with force ∝ (product of sphere 'masses') / (distance between centers)^2. Uses reduction to equivalent central particles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXVI (THEOREMA XXXVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si sphaeræ in progressu a centro ad circumferentiam (quoad materiæ densitatem & vim attractivam) utcunque dissimilares, if in progressu vero per circuitum ad datam omnem a centro distantiam sunt undique similares; & vis attractiva puncti cujusque decrescit in duplicata ratione distantiae corporis attracti: dico quod vis tota, qua huiusmodi sphaera una attrahit aliam, sit reciproce proportionalis quadrato distanticæ centrorum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes previous results to spheres whose density/attractive property vary radially arbitrarily, provided similarity around circles at fixed radius; total mutual attraction between such composite spheres still obeys inverse-square dependence on center separation. Corollaries describe consequences for orbital periods and combined attracting/attracted bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXVII (THEOREMA XXXVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad singula sphaerarum puncta tendant vires centripetæ proportionales distantijs punctorum a corporibus attractis: dico quod vis composita, qua sphaeræ duce se mutuo trahent, est ut distantia inter centra sphaerarum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If elemental attractive forces are proportional to distance (linear law), then the net attraction between spheres is proportional to the distance between their centers (i.e., composite retains linear dependence). Multiple cases give proofs by planar slicing, composition and demonstrate same proportionality for hollow/solid/similar arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEMMA XXIX (geometric infinitesimal lemma)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si describantur centro S circulus quilibet A E B, & centro P circuli duo E F, ef, secantes priorem in E, e, lineamque PS in F, f; & ad Y ?i demittantur perpendicula E D, e d: dico quod, si distantia arcuum E F, e f in infinitum minui intelligatur, ratio ultima lineæ evanescentis D d ad lineam evanescentem F f ea sit, quæ lineæ FK ad lineam P S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A technical geometric lemma about limiting ratios of vanishing arcs and perpendiculars; used in later propositions to relate vanishing surface elements and linear measures when taking infinite limits/infinitesimals.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXIX (THEOREMA XXXIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si superficies ob latitudinem infinite diminutam jamjam evanescens EFfe, convolutione sui circa axem PS, describat solidum sphaericum concavo-convexum, ad cujus particulas singulas aequales tendant aequales vires centripetæ: dico quod vis, qua solidum illud trahit corpusculum situm in P, est in ratione composita ex ratione solidi DEq x Ff, & ratione vis qua particula data in loco Ff traheret idem corpusculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates the attraction exerted by a thin concavo-convex spherical solid (formed by revolving an infinitesimally thin surface) on a point P to geometric products (surface element × height) and to the force that a given particle at a representative location would exert; used to compute contributions of thin shells to net attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXX (THEOREMA XL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Si ad sphaeræ alicujus A B E, centro S descriptæ, particulas singulas æquales tendant æquales vires centripetæ, & ad sphaeræ axem A B, in quo corpusculum aliquod P locatur, erigantur de punctis singulis D perpendicula DE, sphaeræ occurrentia in E, & in ipsis capiantur longitudines DN, quæ sint ut quantitas DE^q & ejus quae sphaeræ particula sita in axe ad distantiam PE exercet in corpusculum P, conjunctim: dico quod vis tota, qua corpusculum P trahitur versus sphaeram, est ut area A N B comprehensa sub axe sphaeræ A B, &f linea curva A N B, quam punctum N perpetuo tangit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a method to reduce the total attraction of a spherical surface on an axis-point to the area under a certain curve ANB; includes lemmas and limiting arguments to express the contribution of each surface 'lamina' as an area element, yielding that total force is proportional to the swept area under ANB. Corollaries cover special cases where elemental centripetal force is constant, inverse-distance, inverse-cube, or general function V.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROPOSITIO LXXXI (PROBLEMA XLI) — measuring area ANB
rubrics_metrics.description: Stantibus jam positis, mensuranda est area A N B. (Gives construction: from P draw tangent PH, drop normal HI, bisect PI in L; establish relation PE^q = PS^q - SE^q - 2PSD etc., then relate DE^q to PS and other quantities to resolve DN into three parts and thus compute the desired area.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A computational geometric problem: provides explicit geometric relations (using tangent, normal, and similarity) to compute the area ANB which represents the integrated attraction according to Prop. LXXX. It continues the analytic-geometric method of the Principia for obtaining closed-form expressions for the net force.
